mnemonic.def: A memory aid that links new information to a pattern, image or phrase that is easier to remember, such as an acronym like ROY G BIV.

method-of-loci.def: A mnemonic that places each item to be remembered at a location along a familiar route, then mentally walks the route to recall them (a memory palace).

chunking.def: Grouping separate pieces of information into larger, meaningful units, so short-term memory can hold more (a phone number as three chunks).

hierarchies.def: Organizing information from broad categories down to specific details, such as an outline, which makes it easier to encode and retrieve.

spacing-effect.def: The finding that study spread out over time leads to better long-term retention than the same amount of study done all at once.

distributed-practice.def: Studying in several sessions spread out over time (spaced practice).

massed-practice.def: Studying in one long session (cramming). It can help on a test soon after, but memories fade faster than with distributed practice.

serial-position.def: The tendency to recall the first and last items in a list better than the middle ones, which gives a U-shaped serial position curve.

primacy.def: Better recall of the first items in a list, because they get more repetition and are encoded into long-term memory.

recency.def: Better recall of the last items in a list, because they are still held in short-term memory when recall begins.
